clue.text: 17 across having doubled lead, end result is tight

indicators.note: the leading letter, read as a Roman numeral, is replaced by one worth twice as much: D is 500, M is 1000

parts.note: the answer to 17 across is DEAN, an academic official

explanation.surface: A footballing scoreline: a side doubles its lead and the final result is tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having doubled lead' treats the D of DEAN as the Roman numeral 500; doubling it gives M, 1000. 'end result is' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean and tight both describe a stingy person who hates spending money.

clue.text: Bloomer showed up, leading to one-all game

parts.note: to show up is to come, past tense came

indicators.note: game in the sense of willing or up for anything, so the letters are ready to be rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football report: someone appeared, and their arrival led to a one-all draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game', meaning willing, is the anagram signal, and 'Bloomer' is not a blunder but something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A camellia is a flowering shrub, and anything that flowers is cryptically a bloomer.

clue.text: Briefly run some cricket team

parts.note: R is the short form of run, as on a cricket scorecard
overs are the sets of six balls that make up a cricket innings

explanation.surface: A brief run-through of a few overs played by a cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: Rovers is a common name for a British football club, such as Blackburn Rovers or Bristol Rovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rovers is the name of many football clubs, so a crossword can call it a team.

clue.text: Stand on this, maybe, and see more? Yes, now encroaching heads shifted

parts.note: see sounds like the letter C, a common crossword shorthand

indicators.note: the letters are shifted around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heads means the first letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A spectator invited to stand and see more, with heads in front of them moving about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' takes the initials of 'Yes, now encroaching' and 'shifted' mixes them with 'more'. The definition alludes to the phrase 'stand on ceremony'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand on ceremony is to insist on formality, so ceremony is something one may stand on.

clue.text: Originally all versions of it described sitting ducks

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning of each word, taking its first letter

explanation.surface: Every early account of the scene featured a row of sitting ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' takes the first letters of the next six words. 'ducks' is the verb: dodges.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question or a blow is to dodge it, which is what someone avoiding it does.

clue.text: A team lacking women in some area

indicators.note: lacking means doing without, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a crew is a team, as in a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A side short of women players somewhere in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes the W for women from the team word.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land measure, so it is a particular amount of area.

clue.text: Smooth passages of play set goal in motion

indicators.note: letters set in motion are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Slick passages of football that set a goal in motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in motion' rearranges SET GOAL. 'play' is musical playing, not football: a legato passage is played smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, legato marks passages to be performed smoothly with notes joined together.

clue.text: After losing first point, nervously receives this?

definitions.text: After losing first point, nervously receives this?

indicators.note: nervously suggests agitated movement, so the remaining letters are jumbled
losing the first one means the earlier of the two matching letters is dropped

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A tennis player, having dropped the first point, nervously awaits the next serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After losing first' drops the first E from RECEIVES, and 'nervously' rearranges RCEIVES. The whole clue also describes a nervous receiver facing the serve.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the receiver faces the opponent's service, the stroke that starts each point.

clue.text: 17 across, a wide man neither side wanted

definitions.note: a dean, the answer to 17 across: W R Inge was the famous Dean of St Paul's

indicators.note: neither side means both outer letters are not wanted and are cut off

parts.note: a winger plays wide on the flank in football

explanation.surface: A footballer who plays out wide that no club wanted to sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neither side wanted' cuts the end letters W and R from WINGER. Dean Inge, the 'gloomy dean' of St Paul's Cathedral, is an old crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: William Ralph Inge was Dean of St Paul's, so he is the classic crossword example of a dean.

clue.text: Former PL team's left wing back dives, missing header and second 12 across?

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-player
taken as written: the Premier League

indicators.note: back means the pair of letters is turned round
the left wing of a word is its left-hand half, its first two letters
missing means the named letters are left out of the word they sit in

parts.note: the header of a word is its first letter, here D

explanation.surface: A former Premier League side's left-wing back takes a dive without heading the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left wing' takes TE from TEAM and 'back' turns it to ET. 'missing header and second' drops D and S from DIVES to leave IVE. 'Balls!' (12 across) is an expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls is a British exclamation of disgust, an example of a mild swear word, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Cooked pig liver, edible starter? That's right

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or messed with, so the letters are reworked
the starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A diner is offered cooked pig liver as a starter and asks if that's correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges PIG LIVER to give PRIVILEG, and 'starter' takes E from 'edible'.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special right or entitlement granted to someone.

clue.text: Rubbish dances by Strictly star

definitions.meaning: Ed ..., the former Labour politician, was a popular contestant on Strictly Come Dancing

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses the routines of a contestant on a TV dance show.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC ballroom dancing contest; the politician Ed Balls appeared on it in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls means nonsense in British slang, grand dancing parties, and the surname of a famous Strictly contestant.

clue.text: Times article on current 'right' way to travel

parts.note: times as in multiplication, two by three
a is the indefinite article
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about the currently correct way to get about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is multiplication: six times seven is six by seven.
explanation.definitionFit: Going by air means flying, one way to travel from place to place.

clue.text: Detective suffering derision from press team

indicators.note: words suffering are damaged or distorted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police detective taking abuse from the press squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from press team' gives the same answer another way: IRON (press) plus SIDE (team). Ironside was a 1960s–70s TV detective in a wheelchair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironside is the title character of an American TV series, a chief of detectives.

clue.text: Slow-paced, lazy speech after tie lost

parts.note: a tie is a draw, a game with level scores
L is the abbreviation for lost, as in a league table

explanation.surface: The commentary goes slow and sluggish after the match ends level and is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: W, D and L, for won, drawn and lost, are the columns of a football league table.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow way of speaking with drawn-out vowels.

clue.text: A delay put back festivity …

indicators.note: put back means the letters are put in reverse order

parts.note: a lag is a delay, as in time lag

explanation.surface: A celebration has been postponed by a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses A LAG. The ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or special entertainment.

clue.text: … the 25th one, perhaps, for Puck?

parts.note: one festivity, carrying on from the last clue: a fair is an example of a gala
Y is the 25th letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Carrying on from the gala: the 25th one, put on for the setter Puck.
explanation.walkthrough: Fairs might be numbered FAIR A, FAIR B and so on, making the 25th FAIR Y. Puck, the setter's pseudonym, is a fairy in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Puck, also called Robin Goodfellow, is a mischievous sprite in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Warning forward respectfully, this may be tugged

parts.note: fore is the warning a golfer shouts
a lock is a forward in rugby

explanation.surface: A warning to a forward, who respectfully tugs something in reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Tugging the forelock, the hair above the forehead, was a traditional show of deference to one's superiors.
explanation.definitionFit: Servants once tugged their forelocks to show respect, the source of the idiom for deference.

clue.text: Academic official content to provide answers

indicators.note: content as a noun means what is contained, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A college official is happy to supply the answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like the adjective 'happy' but is the noun: the contents of PROVIDE ANSWERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior university official in charge of a faculty or of student discipline.

clue.text: Little mischief-makers, half of Devon's swimmers

indicators.note: half of takes the first half of the word that follows

parts.note: lings are fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Little rascals who make up half of the swimmers from a county in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes DEV from DEVON'S. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Devlings are young devils, imps, which are small troublemakers.

clue.text: Can perhaps shoot game here?

definitions.meaning: to ... food is to keep it, canning being one way
ground where game is kept for shooting

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they might be allowed to go shooting on the estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is the verb meaning to put food in tins, not 'is able to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Canning is a way to keep food from spoiling; a game preserve is land kept for hunting.

clue.text: Second team's inside men in charge

parts.note: a crew is a team, so team's gives crews

explanation.surface: A reserve side's dressing room with men in charge of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is slang for in prison, and 'screws' is British slang for prison officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Screws is British slang for prison warders, who are in charge of inmates.

clue.text: Retiring Bengali vicar's well-mannered

indicators.note: Retiring means drawing back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
the 's reads as 'has', so the words that come before it hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shy Bengali clergyman with polite manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like shy, but it reverses the run hidden in 'Bengali vicar'; the 's, read as 'has', says those words contain it. The draft gave the hiding no signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being civil means being polite and courteous, the mark of good manners.

clue.text: Laid-back Corinthian's teammate?

definitions.meaning: Corinthian-... is an English amateur football club, so a ... plays alongside a Corinthian

explanation.walkthrough: Corinthian-Casuals is a south London amateur football club formed by merging the Corinthians and the Casuals.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual means relaxed, and the Casuals were the club that joined the Corinthians.

clue.text: Streetcars, buggies or slow-moving 3?

definitions.meaning: read as Street plus cars: ST plus ROLLERS, slang for Rolls-Royces

explanation.surface: Trams, prams or slow wanderers clogging the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streetcars' splits as ST (street) plus ROLLERS (Rolls-Royce cars). Civil Service Strollers is a Scottish football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Strollers are baby buggies, and people who stroll are wanderers moving at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Watched part of play broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard on air, so the word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: a scene is a part of a play

explanation.surface: Someone watched part of the match on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' is a stage play, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen and watched both describe something observed with the eyes.

clue.text: Some Penguin 'Football Facts'

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Penguin paperback full of football facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Info, short for information, means facts or data.

clue.text: Conveying charge from governing body, with rule essentially being ignored

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which governs English football

indicators.note: the essential middle of the word is ignored, leaving just its outer letters

explanation.surface: A charge passed on by the game's governing body when a rule was broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially being ignored' drops UL from RULE to leave RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fare is the price charged for carrying a passenger on a bus, train or taxi.

clue.text: Sadly bicker about who's first to give name for an Antarctic glacier

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters go round what follows
sadly means in a bad way, so the letters are rearranged
first means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Polar explorers squabble unhappily over who gets to name a glacier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges BICKER into BERICK, which goes 'about' W, the first letter of 'who's'. Berwick is also a town on the England–Scotland border.
explanation.definitionFit: Berwick Glacier is a real glacier in Antarctica, named after the town.

clue.text: Roy's header really annoys 3

definitions.note: like ROVERS (3 down), Rangers is a typical football club name

indicators.note: the header of a word is its first letter, at the top

parts.note: to anger someone is to annoy them greatly

explanation.surface: A footballer named Roy scores with his head, which infuriates the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'header' looks like football but takes R from 'Roy's'. 3 down is ROVERS; Rangers is another such club name, and Berwick Rangers appears in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers and Rovers are both common football club names, so one can stand for the other.
